entities.name: Akkadian Empire
entities.summary: Founded by Sargon of Akkad, often called the first empire, uniting the city-states of Mesopotamia.

entities.name: Old Kingdom of Egypt
entities.summary: The age of the pyramid builders, Dynasties 3 to 8, ruled from Memphis.

entities.name: First Dynasty of Babylon
entities.summary: Babylon's first dynasty; under Hammurabi (c. 1792-1750 BCE) it ruled most of Mesopotamia. Ended by the Hittite sack of Babylon.

entities.name: New Kingdom of Egypt
entities.summary: Dynasties 18 to 20; at its height under Thutmose III it reached from Nubia to the Euphrates.

entities.name: Achaemenid Persian Empire
entities.summary: Founded by Cyrus the Great; under Darius I it stretched from the Indus to Egypt and Thrace. Ended by Alexander.

entities.name: Carthage
entities.summary: Phoenician city whose maritime empire held the western Mediterranean coasts until Rome destroyed it in 146 BCE. Founding date is traditional.

entities.name: Roman Republic
entities.summary: Rome after the expulsion of the kings (traditionally 509 BCE) until Augustus; it conquered Italy, Carthage, Greece, Gaul and much of the east.

entities.name: Roman Empire
entities.summary: From Augustus to the permanent division after Theodosius I. Greatest extent at Trajan's death in 117 CE.

entities.name: Western Roman Empire
entities.summary: The western half after 395; it ended when Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus in 476.

entities.name: Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire
entities.summary: The eastern half, ruled from Constantinople until the Ottoman conquest of 1453.

entities.name: Empire of Alexander
entities.summary: Macedon under Alexander the Great, who conquered the Achaemenid Empire and reached the Indus.

entities.name: Seleucid Empire
entities.summary: The largest successor state of Alexander's empire, from Anatolia to Bactria at first; annexed by Rome in 63 BCE.

entities.name: Ptolemaic Kingdom
entities.summary: Egypt under the Macedonian Ptolemies, ruled from Alexandria until Cleopatra VII and the Roman conquest.

entities.name: Maurya Empire
entities.summary: Founded by Chandragupta Maurya; under Ashoka it covered most of the Indian subcontinent.

entities.name: Qin dynasty
entities.summary: The first imperial dynasty of China, founded when the state of Qin completed the unification in 221 BCE.

entities.name: Han dynasty
entities.summary: Western Han (202 BCE-9 CE) and Eastern Han (25-220 CE), interrupted by Wang Mang's Xin dynasty.

entities.name: Xin dynasty
entities.summary: Wang Mang's interregnum between Western and Eastern Han.

entities.name: State of Han (Warring States)
entities.summary: One of the seven Warring States, conquered by Qin in 230 BCE. Not the Han dynasty.

entities.name: Tang dynasty
entities.summary: Tang China, whose capital Chang'an was the eastern end of the Silk Road; weakened after the An Lushan rebellion (755-763).

entities.name: Abbasid Caliphate
entities.summary: The caliphate ruled from Baghdad (founded 762) until the Mongol sack of 1258; its effective power shrank from the 9th century.

entities.name: Song dynasty
entities.summary: Northern Song (960-1127) at Kaifeng and Southern Song (1127-1279) at Hangzhou, ended by the Mongol conquest.

entities.name: Mongol Empire
entities.summary: From Genghis Khan's proclamation in 1206; after 1260 a set of khanates. Shown to 1368, when the Yuan dynasty was driven from China.

entities.name: Mali Empire
entities.summary: West African empire founded by Sundiata Keita; under Mansa Musa it controlled the gold trade across the Sahara.

entities.name: Ottoman Empire
entities.summary: From Osman I to the abolition of the sultanate in 1922; it took Constantinople in 1453 and besieged Vienna in 1683.

entities.name: Ming dynasty
entities.summary: Founded by Zhu Yuanzhang after the Yuan; it sent Zheng He's fleets into the Indian Ocean (1405-1433).

entities.name: Aztec Empire (Triple Alliance)
entities.summary: The alliance of Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan; it fell to Spanish and allied forces in 1521.

entities.name: Inca Empire
entities.summary: Expanded from Cusco under Pachacuti; the largest state of the pre-Columbian Americas. Atahualpa was executed by the Spanish in 1533.

entities.name: Mughal Empire
entities.summary: Founded by Babur after the first battle of Panipat; at its greatest extent under Aurangzeb, nominal after the 18th century, ended by the British in 1857.

entities.name: Qing dynasty
entities.summary: The Manchu dynasty, which took Beijing in 1644 and reached its greatest extent in the 18th century.

entities.name: United States
entities.summary: Declared independence in 1776; recognised to the Mississippi in 1783; Louisiana Purchase 1803; reached the Pacific by 1848.

entities.name: Jericho
entities.summary: One of the oldest continuously inhabited sites; walled by c. 8000 BCE.

entities.name: Catalhoyuk
entities.summary: Large Neolithic town on the Konya plain.

entities.name: Beidha
entities.summary: Pre-Pottery Neolithic village near Petra.

entities.name: Eridu
entities.summary: Considered by the Sumerians the first city.

entities.name: Uruk
entities.summary: Sumerian city where proto-cuneiform writing appears c. 3200 BCE.

entities.name: Ur
entities.summary: Sumerian city, capital of the Third Dynasty of Ur.

entities.name: Girsu
entities.summary: Capital of the state of Lagash (also listed as Lagash).

entities.name: Mari
entities.summary: City on the Euphrates destroyed by Hammurabi.

entities.name: Akkad
entities.summary: Sargon's capital; its site has never been found (placed near Sippar).

entities.name: Isin
entities.summary: Capital of the Isin dynasty after Ur's fall.

entities.name: Larsa
entities.summary: Rival of Isin, conquered by Hammurabi.

entities.name: Nippur
entities.summary: The religious centre of Sumer.

entities.name: Umma
entities.summary: Sumerian city-state, rival of Lagash.

entities.name: Mohenjo-daro
entities.summary: City of the mature Indus civilization.

entities.name: Memphis
entities.summary: Capital of the Old Kingdom, at the apex of the Nile delta.

entities.name: Abydos
entities.summary: Early royal burial ground of Egypt.

entities.name: Thebes
entities.summary: Capital of the Middle and New Kingdoms (Waset; modern Luxor).

entities.name: Avaris
entities.summary: Hyksos capital in the eastern delta.

entities.name: Pi-Ramesses
entities.summary: Ramesses II's capital, beside Avaris.

entities.name: Babylon
entities.summary: Capital of Hammurabi and of Nebuchadnezzar II.

entities.name: Nimrud (Kalhu)
entities.summary: Assyrian capital under Ashurnasirpal II.

entities.name: Nineveh
entities.summary: Assyrian capital, destroyed in 612 BCE.

entities.name: Yinxu (Anyang)
entities.summary: Last capital of the Shang dynasty.

entities.name: Qiyi (Zhouyuan)
entities.summary: Early Zhou homeland at the foot of Mount Qi.

entities.name: Haojing
entities.summary: Western Zhou capital near modern Xi'an.

entities.name: Luoyang
entities.summary: Capital of Eastern Zhou, Eastern Han and later dynasties (Luoyi, Chengzhou).

entities.name: Linzi
entities.summary: Capital of the state of Qi.

entities.name: Pataliputra
entities.summary: Capital of Magadha and of the Maurya Empire (modern Patna).

entities.name: Alexandria
entities.summary: Founded by Alexander in 331 BCE; capital of Ptolemaic Egypt.

entities.name: Alexandria Eschate
entities.summary: 'Alexandria the Furthest', founded by Alexander on the Syr Darya (modern Khujand).

entities.name: Carthage
entities.summary: Phoenician city; destroyed 146 BCE, refounded as a Roman colony, destroyed again in 698.

entities.name: Rome
entities.summary: Founded, by tradition, in 753 BCE; capital of the Republic and the Empire.

entities.name: Chang'an
entities.summary: Capital of Western Han and Tang (rebuilt as Daxing under the Sui); modern Xi'an.

entities.name: Ctesiphon
entities.summary: Parthian and Sasanian capital on the Tigris.

entities.name: Constantinople
entities.summary: Greek Byzantium, refounded by Constantine in 330 as Constantinople; Istanbul under the Ottomans.

entities.name: Nanjing
entities.summary: Capital of the Southern dynasties (Jiankang) and of the early Ming (Yingtian).

entities.name: Baghdad
entities.summary: Founded in 762 by the caliph al-Mansur as the Abbasid capital.

entities.name: Cordoba
entities.summary: Capital of the Umayyad emirate and caliphate of al-Andalus.

entities.name: Kaifeng
entities.summary: Capital of the Northern Song.

entities.name: Merv
entities.summary: Oasis city on the Silk Road, sacked by the Mongols in 1221.

entities.name: Cairo
entities.summary: Founded by the Fatimids in 969.

entities.name: Fez
entities.summary: Founded by the Idrisids at the end of the 8th century.

entities.name: Hangzhou
entities.summary: Capital of the Southern Song (Lin'an).

entities.name: Beijing
entities.summary: Jin Zhongdu, Yuan Dadu (Khanbaliq), then Ming and Qing Beijing.

entities.name: Ayutthaya
entities.summary: Capital of the Ayutthaya kingdom of Siam until its destruction in 1767.

entities.name: Tokyo
entities.summary: Edo, the Tokugawa capital, renamed Tokyo in 1868.

entities.name: London
entities.summary: Roman Londinium, founded c. 47 CE.

entities.name: New York
entities.summary: Dutch New Amsterdam, English New York from 1664.

entities.name: Athens
entities.summary: Birthplace of Athenian democracy (Cleisthenes, 508 BCE).

entities.name: Persepolis
entities.summary: Ceremonial capital of the Achaemenids, burned by Alexander.

entities.name: Susa
entities.summary: Elamite city and Achaemenid capital, end of the Royal Road.

entities.name: Tenochtitlan
entities.summary: Aztec capital on Lake Texcoco; Mexico City after 1521.

entities.name: Cusco
entities.summary: Capital of the Inca Empire.

entities.name: Timbuktu
entities.summary: Trans-Saharan trading and scholarly city.

entities.name: Samarkand
entities.summary: Sogdian city at the heart of the Silk Road.

entities.name: Dunhuang
entities.summary: Han garrison at the western end of the Hexi corridor; the Mogao caves.

entities.name: Muziris
entities.summary: Port on the Malabar coast in the Roman pepper trade (site uncertain).

entities.name: Antioch
entities.summary: Seleucid capital and one of the great cities of the Roman east.

entities.name: Palmyra
entities.summary: Caravan city of the Syrian desert.

entities.name: Guangzhou
entities.summary: Port of the maritime Silk Road (Canton).

entities.name: Venice
entities.summary: Maritime republic at the western end of the medieval spice trade.

entities.name: Malacca
entities.summary: Sultanate commanding the strait between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea.

entities.name: Xianyang
entities.summary: Capital of Qin, burned in 206 BCE.

entities.name: Sargon of Akkad
entities.summary: Founder of the Akkadian Empire.

entities.name: Hammurabi
entities.summary: King of Babylon (reigned c. 1792-1750 BCE), author of the law code.

entities.name: Cyrus the Great
entities.summary: Founder of the Achaemenid Empire (reigned 559-530 BCE).

entities.name: Alexander the Great
entities.summary: King of Macedon from 336 BCE, conqueror of the Persian Empire; died at Babylon in 323 BCE.

entities.name: Ashoka
entities.summary: Maurya emperor (reigned c. 268-232 BCE) who turned to Buddhism after the Kalinga war.

entities.name: Qin Shi Huang
entities.summary: King of Qin who unified China in 221 BCE and took the title of First Emperor.

entities.name: Zhang Qian
entities.summary: Han envoy whose missions to Central Asia (138-126 BCE, 119-115 BCE) opened official contact along the Silk Road.

entities.name: Augustus
entities.summary: First Roman emperor, from 27 BCE until his death in 14 CE.

entities.name: Trajan
entities.summary: Roman emperor (98-117) under whom the empire reached its greatest extent.

entities.name: Ban Chao
entities.summary: Eastern Han general who restored Chinese control of the Tarim basin.

entities.name: Genghis Khan
entities.summary: Founder of the Mongol Empire, proclaimed in 1206.

entities.name: Marco Polo
entities.summary: Venetian who travelled to Kublai Khan's China (1271-1295).

entities.name: Mansa Musa
entities.summary: Ruler of Mali whose pilgrimage to Mecca (1324-25) displayed its gold wealth.

entities.name: Zheng He
entities.summary: Ming admiral who led seven voyages into the Indian Ocean (1405-1433).

entities.name: Cuneiform writing
entities.summary: Writing on clay, developed from proto-cuneiform tablets at Uruk c. 3200 BCE.

entities.name: Paper
entities.summary: Its invention is traditionally credited to Cai Lun in 105 CE (earlier fragments exist); it reached the Islamic world in the 8th century.

entities.name: Movable type
entities.summary: Ceramic movable type of Bi Sheng (c. 1040), described by Shen Kuo.

entities.name: Printing press
entities.summary: Gutenberg's press with metal type at Mainz, c. 1450.

entities.name: Steam engine (Watt)
entities.summary: James Watt's separate condenser (patented 1769), central to the Industrial Revolution.

events.name: Gobekli Tepe's stone enclosures built
events.summary: Monumental stone circles raised by hunter-gatherers, before farming took hold.

events.name: Jericho's wall and tower
events.summary: A stone wall and tower around a settlement of the Pre-Pottery Neolithic.

events.name: Catalhoyuk settled
events.summary: A densely packed Neolithic town of mud-brick houses.

events.name: Proto-cuneiform tablets at Uruk
events.summary: The earliest writing, used for accounts in the temple economy.

events.name: Great Pyramid of Giza

events.name: Sargon founds the Akkadian Empire

events.name: Mature Indus civilization

events.name: Code of Hammurabi

events.name: Battle of Kadesh

events.name: Zhou conquest of Shang

events.name: Carthage founded (traditional)

events.name: First recorded Olympic Games

events.name: Founding of Rome (traditional)
events.summary: Varro's traditional date for Romulus's foundation.

events.name: Fall of Nineveh
events.summary: Babylonians and Medes destroy the Assyrian capital.

events.name: Cyrus founds the Persian Empire

events.name: Cyrus takes Babylon

events.name: Roman Republic established

stories.title: The Silk Road
stories.summary: Two thousand years of exchange between China, Central Asia, Persia and the Mediterranean, overland and by sea.

chapters.title: An envoy goes west
chapters.text: In 138 BCE the Han emperor Wudi sends Zhang Qian west to find allies against the Xiongnu. Captured for ten years, he returns in 126 BCE with reports of horses, cities and markets in Central Asia. Han armies then open the Hexi corridor towards Dunhuang.

chapters.title: Rome and Han at either end
chapters.text: By the 1st century CE silk worn in Rome had passed through Parthian and Kushan hands. Neither empire knew the other well; the Book of the Later Han records one embassy from 'Daqin' in 166, arriving by sea.

chapters.title: Tang and the caliphate
chapters.text: Tang Chang'an and Abbasid Baghdad anchor the route. After the Battle of Talas in 751 papermaking spreads west through Samarkand.

chapters.title: Under the Mongols
chapters.text: From the 1250s one empire and its khanates span the route, and Venetians such as Marco Polo cross Asia to Kublai Khan's court.

chapters.title: The sea takes over
chapters.text: Ming fleets under Zheng He reach East Africa (1405-1433); in 1498 Vasco da Gama arrives in India by sea, and the long-distance trade shifts to the oceans.

stories.title: Rome, from Latium to Constantinople
stories.summary: The growth of the Roman state from a city in Latium to an empire of 5 million km2, and its division.

chapters.title: A republic in Latium
chapters.text: By tradition the Romans expel their last king in 509 BCE. Over two centuries they absorb the peoples of Italy.

chapters.title: Carthage
chapters.text: Three wars with Carthage (264-146 BCE) give Rome Sicily, Sardinia, Spain and Africa; Hannibal crosses the Alps in 218 BCE.

chapters.title: Gaul and the east
chapters.text: Caesar conquers Gaul (58-50 BCE); Pompey annexes Syria. Octavian's victory at Actium brings Egypt in 30 BCE.

chapters.title: The greatest extent
chapters.text: When Trajan dies in 117 the empire reaches from Britain to Mesopotamia, about 5 million km2 by Taagepera's estimate.

chapters.title: Division and survival
chapters.text: From 395 the empire is ruled in two halves. The west ends in 476; the east, ruled from Constantinople, lasts until 1453.

stories.title: The first cities
stories.summary: From Neolithic villages to the cities of Sumer and Egypt.

chapters.title: Before farming
chapters.text: At Gobekli Tepe, hunter-gatherers raise stone enclosures around 9500 BCE; Jericho is walled by 8000 BCE.

chapters.title: Uruk
chapters.text: By 3200 BCE Uruk is the largest settlement in the world, and its scribes keep accounts in the first writing.

chapters.title: Kings and laws
chapters.text: Egypt is unified c. 3100 BCE; Sargon builds the first empire c. 2334 BCE; Hammurabi's code is set up c. 1754 BCE.
